plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the FRED Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) series page, focusing on data visualization interactivity, metadata clarity, and responsive layout stability.
plan.summary: The exploration will focus on the single-page application structure of `index.html`. It begins by validating the core chart interactions (time range toggles, tooltips, recession shading), moves to secondary views (data table, graph editing tools), and concludes with a rigorous mobile viewport check to address pre-identified tap target issues. Since no other HTML pages exist, depth is prioritized over breadth.
assumptions: The site is a Single Page Application (SPA) or static mockup where 'navigation' triggers state changes rather than full page reloads.
The 'Edit Graph', 'Download', and 'Share' controls trigger modals or dropdowns that are not visible in the initial DOM scan but are critical for user tasks.
The 'View as data table' toggle replaces the chart canvas with an HTML table, requiring validation of data parity.
risk_hotspots: Chart Tooltip: Hovering over data points must accurately display date/value pairs without flickering.
Recession Shading: Visual distinction between recession periods (gray bars) and the data line must be clear.
Mobile Tap Targets: Prescan identified multiple elements <44px; navigation and chart controls need verification on mobile.
Date Range Inputs: Manual entry in 'From/To' fields must validate against the dataset bounds (1948-2026).

phases.title: Core Chart Interaction & State Management
phases.objective: Validate the primary data visualization flow, ensuring time-range toggles update the view correctly and tooltips provide accurate context.
key_checks: Click '1Y', '5Y', '10Y', and 'Max' toggles; verify chart axis and data points update accordingly.
Hover over multiple data points across different eras (e.g., 1980s peak, 2020 drop) to test tooltip accuracy and positioning.
Verify recession shading (gray vertical bars) aligns correctly with historical downturns.
Test manual date range inputs ('From'/'To') with valid and invalid dates.
exit_criteria: All time-range toggles visually update the chart.
No console errors during state transitions.

phases.title: Secondary Views & Action Controls
phases.objective: Explore adjacent features including the data table view, graph customization, and export options.
key_checks: Toggle 'View as data table'; verify tabular data matches the visual chart trends.
Click 'Edit Graph' to identify available customization options (line style, colors, etc.).
Click 'Download' and 'Share' to verify modal/dialog behavior and copy-to-clipboard functionality.
Review the 'Notes' and 'Metadata' section for readability and completeness.
exit_criteria: Data table renders without layout breakage.
Action buttons (Download/Share/Edit) trigger expected UI responses (modals/dropdowns).

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Address prescan warnings regarding small tap targets and ensure usability on narrow viewports.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/12).
Attempt to close the maintenance banner and use main navigation links; measure ease of tapping.
Verify chart interactivity on touch devices (tap-to-hover vs. scroll behavior).
Check if the 'Edit Graph' and 'Download' buttons remain accessible or collapse into a menu.
Validate that text in the metadata section does not overflow or become illegible.
exit_criteria: Critical controls are tappable without zooming.
No horizontal scrolling issues on the main content area.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all chart toggles, view modes, and action buttons
coverage_targets.mobile: Full regression of Phase 1 and 2 checks on mobile viewport

notes: The prescan indicates a 'maintenance notice' banner. Ensure this is dismissed or accounted for in layout calculations.
Since there is only one HTML file, 'navigation' tests should focus on internal anchors (e.g., #mainContent) and dynamic state changes.
Pay special attention to the 'Units' and 'Frequency' metadata, as these are crucial for correct data interpretation in financial contexts.
